newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says rumours of EMU delay "absurd".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says rumours of EMU delay "absurd".

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi rejected as "absurd" on Wednesday market rumours that Italian entry into European monetary and economic union (EMU) might be delayed.
"These are absurd rumours, devoid of any foundation, which make no sense whatsoever," Prodi said in response to a reporter's question about the rumours.
"The government programme has already been outlined," Prodi said. "We have even proposed moving forward the (1998) budget."
Prodi said the government had made EMU entry a priority and added: "We will meet the required criteria".
"Our entry into monetary union is increasingly important and I don't see any elements that could put this process into doubt," he said.
"I can't understand where these rumours come from," he said.
Prodi has repeatedly reaffirmed Italy's intention to be among founder members of the new euro from 1999.
He has proposed moving the deadline for parliamentary passage of the 1998 budget forward by four months to mid-August to boost confidence.

On Tuesday Juergen Stark, State Secretary at the German Finance Ministry, said that some aspirants should forsake the political prestige of entering EMU at the outset, adding there were countries whose economic structures were not sufficiently prepared to take part.
Stark, number two to Finance Minister Theo Waigel and a hard-liner on monetary union, did not name names, but his comments appeared directed at countries like Italy or Spain.

Italy's state auditor, Andrea Monorchio, said earlier on Wednesday that he was convinced Italy would achieve a 1997 budget deficit-GDP ratio of three percent, one of the key criteria for EMU membership.
